story: One does not simply calculate the absolute value
text: > The bits of a float as an integer literal are proportional to its log2 value (plus a constant), … I watched a video[0] a while back about that. Once that coincidence(?) was explained, Q_rsqrt finally made sense. [0]: [VIDEO] (~20 minutes)

Apparently the bit pattern of a float interpreted as an int is sorta-kinda it's own logarithm, which is why the famous fast inverse square root from quake 3 works: log(x^-½) = -½log(x) =~ -log(x) >> 1. This video is approachable and explains it pretty well: [VIDEO]
